Welcome to the good side of tech 👋
You might have heard about us, but with a different name: Doctoralia. It all started 12 years ago when we asked ourselves: is anyone in healthcare thinking about patients? We jumped in and we empowered patients by giving them access to leave and read reviews about their visit.

We then provided doctors with the technology to manage bookings easily and save time, so they could devote themselves to what they always wanted: treating patients. And today is the day in which we ask you: wanna join us in the next step of making the healthcare experience more human?
Docplanner at scale
We are leaders in 13 countries so far, and more than 90 million patients trust us every month. 300k+ specialists believe in us and our product, and so do leading venture capital funds such as Point Nine Capital, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and One Peak Partners. And yet, employing over 2.500 people all over the globe, we managed to keep the startup-mindset we started with over 10 years ago.
How does Docplanner Tech fit here?
At Docplanner Tech we are a diverse group of over 300 people working in Engineering, Data, and Product teams. We are responsible for building the product for all locations. Many of us have been here for over 5 years, yet we still welcome each new person with great joy and excitement.
We could tell you about us, but we will let our reviews on Glassdoor speak for themselves. In case you’d like to see how it feels to be 100% yourself at work, here’s a video of us .
And why should you join us?
Because it feels good to tell your family and your friends how you made the world a little bit better. You go to bed knowing that what you do matters, and that your talents align with your beliefs.
We want to make the healthcare experience more human, and that starts with you being you. We believe that taking the diversity of human experience into account makes a better healthcare experience for all . We’re not just different: we embrace diversity. We will encourage you to come to work your whole self, and that includes not coming to the office at all if you prefer not to, as we're 100% remote friendly.
Job Description
Docplanner is fostering the reinvention of product development, and above all transforming how we approach coding with AI. We are looking for a Senior Engineering Manager who will lead this transformation from the front lines, while owning the Patient Engagement area.
You will lead a group of 7–9 engineers organised into several small squads, each owning a distinct business goal. Your job is to keep those squads fast, focused and genuinely AI-native, and to stay hands-on in the code yourself. This is not a hands-off role.
What makes it different is the mindset it asks for. AI-assisted coding is already part of how we work; the next level is turning it into a step change in how quickly we go from an idea to a validated answer. That takes a founder's instincts i.e. running cheap experiments to test assumptions, dropping what doesn't work, and repointing a squad when the user need turns out to be different from what we assumed.
The scope is meaningful: Patient Engagement initiatives that directly impact how people interact with their healthcare, focusing on engagement, retention and continuity of care. These aren't just features; they're tools that help real people better manage their health.
What Success Looks Like in 6 Months
You're making deliberate trade-offs between foundational work and fast experimentation, and you can explain the calls: what you invested in, what you deliberately deferred, and why.
The engineers reporting to you are visibly growing, engaged, and raising their own bar.
Your squads are delivering faster and at higher quality, with AI-enabled workflows becoming the default way of working.
You're personally shipping. Writing code and delivering features at a healthy, steady pace. Setting the bar for what good AI-enabled development looks like in practice.
Patient Engagement is showing tangible improvements in engagement, retention and continuity of care.
But the real indicator of success? Other teams start knocking on your door. They want to understand your workflows, adopt your practices, and replicate your results. Not in theory, but in ways that actually ship better patient experiences, faster.

Drive Technical Leadership & Take AI Usage to the Next Level
Lead 7–9 senior engineers across several small squads, each owning distinct business goals. Owning their growth, performance and hiring, and keeping each squad clear on the outcome it's accountable for.
Track and communicate impact with concrete metrics such as delivery speed, quality, developer satisfaction and product outcomes.
Set the direction on where to invest: which foundations are worth building, which bets are worth a fast experiment, and when to pivot a squad based on what the users actually need.
Partner closely with Product and Design to solve real patient problems end to end.
Push AI-assisted development well past where we are today in Patient Engagement. Prove the practices work, then help scale them across engineering.
Influence the wider Engineering community by example. Sharing what works, partnering rather than mandating, and helping teams adopt AI-enabled ways of working.
Lead Through Code
Experiment with and establish AI-powered development workflows, then teach others through direct, hands-on demonstration
Solve real patient engagement and continuity challenges through hands-on coding, using cutting-edge AI development tools to demonstrate new possibilities.
Prototype and build solutions that showcase AI-enabled development practices in patient-facing products.
Work directly in your teams' codebases. It means not just reviewing, but implementing features and architectural changes.

In a sentence: someone who can code the future while being passionate about delivering real impact to users and inspiring others to follow.
You operate with a founder mindset. You move from idea to experiment quickly, validate with real users, and change direction without ego when the evidence says you should
You've led multiple teams or squads at once, and you know how to keep each one focused on its own outcome without becoming a bottleneck.
You thrive in ambiguity and enjoy being the first to try something new, figure out what works, and help others navigate the same path.
You measure what matters and iterate relentlessly, focused on building software that is faster, better and more impactful.
You bring solid hands-on experience using AI to accelerate software development, improving how code is written, reviewed and refactored, with strong judgment on when to rely on AI versus traditional approaches.
People naturally follow your technical lead because you consistently deliver results and raise the bar for those around you.
You genuinely enjoy teaching and mentoring, whether through pairing, retrospectives, or helping others level up.
Bonus points if you've worked at scale, but we care more about how you think, the impact you drive, and your focus on meaningful user outcomes than the size of your previous company.

Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our wireless network engineering team - the team that keeps one of the world's largest private IoT networks connected. Over a million devices across New Zealand, Australia, the US and Canada, spanning LoRa, cellular, and satellite direct-to-device, running on remote infrastructure in some of the hardest terrain there is.
This isn't a pure delivery or pure people role. You'll be in the work: shaping the network architecture, weighing in on spectrum strategy and link budgets, reviewing the automation that runs our tower fleet, and helping your team do the best work of their careers. You'll need to hold the technical bar high while creating the space for others to grow.
We're solving connectivity problems that haven't been solved before - keeping livestock connected hundreds of kilometres from the nearest town, where there's often no coverage at all. It's a role that demands absolute ownership: someone who can take a blurry problem, create clarity, and lead a team to nail it.

s.h: THE KIND OF PROBLEMS YOUR TEAM SOLVES
s.t:
Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. The wireless network team owns the connectivity layer everything else depends on:
Keeping over a million collars connected across LoRa, cellular, and satellite direct-to-device - in valleys, over ridgelines, and far beyond the edge of conventional coverage.
Planning coverage with real RF engineering: link budgets, path loss modelling, antenna selection, and spectrum strategy across multiple regulatory regimes.
Running a fleet of thousands of remote towers with zero-touch provisioning, configuration automation, and remote diagnostics - a truck roll to a hill-country site is expensive, so software has to do the work.
Squeezing every byte: our devices are power and bandwidth constrained, so protocol efficiency and data optimisation directly shape the product.
Making network health visible - turning telemetry from millions of radio links into signals engineers and field teams can act on.
Every team here ships systems that have to work in a paddock, not just a browser tab. As an engineering manager at Halter, you're in the work, not above it: coaching engineers, shaping the technical bets, and staying hands-on.

Lead a team of wireless network engineers - supporting their growth, giving great feedback, running performance conversations, and helping them focus on what matters.
Own the technical direction and delivery of the network: architecture, reliability, and scalability across collar-to-tower-to-cloud connectivity.
Stay close to the technical details - spectrum allocation and compliance, LoRa and cellular behaviour, tower infrastructure, fleet configuration automation, and the software tooling that ties it together - and bring a strong point of view.
Own network reliability outcomes: uptime, incident response, and the on-call practices that keep a 24/7 physical network healthy without burning the team out.
Drive tower deployment and coverage strategy as we scale into new regions - site selection, RF planning, and delivery of critical infrastructure.
Hire and grow the team. Wireless network engineering is a rare skill mix, and you'll be building a world-class bench of it.
Work closely with firmware, backend, hardware, and field operations to shape what we build, not just how. You'll be in the room when requirements are fuzzy and you'll help make them clear.
Back engineering-led initiatives and look for opportunities to use AI tools to accelerate development or unlock entirely new ways of working.
Get out on farm. Deep domain knowledge matters and you'll be expected to develop it.
Contribute to the broader engineering culture and practices that make Halter a great place to build.

Have led engineers directly - performance conversations, mentoring, hiring, the lot.
Have strong wireless networking fundamentals - you're credible on spectrum allocation, path loss, link budgets, and antenna behaviour, and can hold a high technical bar with specialists in these areas.
Have hands-on experience with LoRa/LoRaWAN, cellular, or other long-range wireless technologies deployed at scale.
Understand platform infrastructure - configuration management (Ansible or similar), fleet automation, and what it takes to run thousands of remote devices reliably.
Are comfortable in code (Go, Python, C++) - enough to review the team's tooling, dig into a data question yourself, and keep your technical judgement sharp.
Know how to shape and structure work without being overly prescriptive, and balance speed with quality.
Stay calm under pressure, have a low ego, and can rally a team through tough or complex work - including incidents on live infrastructure.
You've worked in fast-moving startups, seen growth, and tackled ambiguous problem spaces.
Bonus points for experience with satellite direct-to-device or NTN, spectrum regulatory work (FCC, ACMA, ComReg, or similar), embedded systems or firmware exposure, and building or operating infrastructure in harsh, remote environments.

Build with us

Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow – with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.
With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.

Analytics Engineering at Mollie is a craft we take seriously. As Analytics Engineering Manager for RevOps, you sit at the intersection of people leadership and technical craft, responsible for both the growth of the Analytics Engineers you manage and the quality of the work they produce.

You will lead a team of approximately six direct reports, spanning the RevOps domain and analysts in adjacent domains such Planning & Analysis and Mollie Connect, making sure the craft is well represented and well applied across all of them.
The RevOps domain is central to how Mollie understands and demonstrates its commercial performance. You will own the domain metrics together with your team, ensuring that what gets measured actually gets used, and that stakeholders across the business can see the impact of the work being done.

Beyond the domain itself, you will help shape how Analytics Engineering as a craft evolves at Mollie, setting standards, improving ways of working, and making sure the teams you support know how to get the most out of the craft.
This is a role for someone who is equally comfortable coaching a direct report through a tricky career conversation and reviewing a dbt model for quality. You will partner closely with accountable leads on planning and roadmaps, advocate for the craft with non-technical stakeholders, and drive initiatives that raise the bar across the whole Analytics Engineering community at Mollie.
What you'll ship
A consistent, high-quality Analytics Engineering practice across the RevOps domain and supported adjacent teams, with clear standards, documented ways of working, and a team that applies them reliably
A well-maintained and trusted set of RevOps domain metrics that give stakeholders a clear, consistent view of business performance and commercial impact
A structured performance management cycle for your direct reports, including regular feedback, meaningful reviews, and development goals that are set and tracked in genuine partnership with accountable leads
Craft-level initiatives that improve how Analytics Engineers work across teams, from tooling and best practices to knowledge sharing and onboarding
A planning and prioritisation process that supports accountable leads effectively, with Analytics Engineering work scoped, sequenced, and delivered to a high standard
A team of Analytics Engineers who are growing in their craft, supported through coaching, mentoring, and learning opportunities that are tailored to where each person wants to go

At least five years of experience in an analytics or analytics engineering environment, with a background in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, engineering, econometrics, or a related field
Experience leading or managing analytics engineers or analysts, with a track record of supporting people through feedback, development conversations, and performance cycles, and a genuine interest in helping others grow
The ability to partner effectively with commercial teams such as sales, marketing, and revenue operations, translating between what the business needs and what the craft can deliver
Solid hands-on experience with SQL and a cloud data warehouse, with the ability to review and contribute to technical work directly
Practical experience with dbt or an equivalent data modelling tool, and a clear understanding of what good data modelling looks like in practice
Familiarity with a BI tool that includes a semantic layer, such as Looker or similar, and an understanding of how these tools connect to downstream business use cases
Grow your way
At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.
You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.
No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

The Data Modeling team builds and maintains the core data models and metrics that power decision-making across Mural. We are part of the Data Organization and focus on creating shared, reusable data models that represent key product and business concepts and are used across the company.
Our work supports internal analytics, customer insight reports embedded in the product, and AI/ML model training. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Platform, Business Analytics, Data Science, and Analytics Engineering to ensure the company is working from consistent definitions, high data quality, and reliable data availability.
We are a small, high-leverage team focused on building durable data foundations rather than one-off solutions.

You will own the delivery and evolution of Mural’s core data models and shared metrics, with a strong focus on data quality, reliability, and availability.
This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not build stakeholder-specific data marts or ad-hoc analyses. Instead, you will focus on building foundational, reusable data models and metric definitions that support many use cases across the company.
Your success will be measured by how widely trusted, consistently available, and broadly reused the data models and metrics you own are across teams such as Business Analytics, in-product insights, and ML.

Partner across teams: Work closely with Product to define foundational product concepts, with Data Platform on architecture and reliability, and with Business Analytics, Data Science, ML, and in-product insights teams as key consumers
Set technical direction: Make pragmatic decisions about modeling standards, architecture, orchestration (Airflow/Astronomer), and tooling that balance near-term delivery with long-term maintainability

Leadership experience: 2+ years leading or formally managing data professionals
Strong foundational data modeling experience: 6+ years building and owning shared, reusable core data models in modern data platforms
Experience supporting SaaS businesses: Familiarity with product usage, and customer data common to SaaS environments
Hands-on technical depth: Advanced SQL, strong Python, experience with Spark, and comfort working in a modern lakehouse environment (e.g., Databricks)
Operational mindset: Experience designing for data quality, reliability, and availability, including workflow orchestration with Airflow or Astronomer
Reuse-first thinking: Proven ability to build foundational models and metric definitions that support multiple use cases rather than one-off data marts
Systems awareness: Understanding of performance, cost, governance, security, and compliance considerations for shared data
Collaborative approach: Ability to partner effectively with Product, Data Platform, Business Analytics, Engineering, and Data Science teams
Pragmatic delivery mindset: You know when to ship and when to invest in durability
Interest in AI-assisted development: You actively explore AI tools to improve how you and your team build and maintain data models

Experience supporting data used for AI/ML model training
Background working on a data infrastructure or data platform team

About Pleo
Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.
The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.
Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high.

With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

Joining our team as an Engineering Manager places you at the forefront of advancing our technical excellence and innovation. You will be part of a knowledgeable team of leaders representing various technical areas. In this role, you will report directly to our Product Lead , while your closest day-to-day collaborator will be the Product Manager supervising the same cross-functional teams.
You’re responsible for delivery and outcomes across multiple engineering teams. In this role, you are a developer at heart but a leader by choice. You are someone who has lived the dev life, understands the technical trenches, but realized your true calling is empowering other developers to do their best work.

You foster the environment in which engineers perform at their best and grow both as individuals and as a team. You do so by serving as a mentor and coach, ensuring each team member is clear on expectations, making sure our processes help rather than hinder, and working closely with engineers to ensure we are building high-quality software.
Your Leadership Style
We are looking for a leader with an empowering management style—someone who knows how to motivate a team, establish a clear sense of direction, and build a resilient team spirit. You lead by enabling others rather than micromanaging, creating an environment where engineers feel ownership over their work.
Balancing empathy with high standards, you know how to keep the team accountable to their commitments and quality benchmarks. We want an engineering manager whose team will be standing on the top of the mountain with them—celebrating a shared victory together, energized by the journey rather than left behind exhausted on the path below. You will help your team(s) through the journey of becoming high-performing, building deep trust among the members, and helping them fine-tune their processes.

Vision & Alignment: Work closely with the Product Lead and Product Managers to set a clear vision and direction for your group of product teams. Align technical direction within your area with the overall technology direction of the company.
Direct Management & Coaching: Directly manage, mentor, and oversee Engineers (and Tech Leads). Focus heavily on continuous training, upskilling, and professional growth for your team members.
Accelerate AI Adoption: Evaluate, introduce, and integrate modern AI development tools and methodologies into the team's daily routines to safely boost developer velocity and innovation.
Drive Quality & Mindset: Cultivate a customer-centric, solution-oriented mindset while holding a high standard for clean, high-quality, and scalable software delivery.
Continuous Improvement: Continuously improve the environment, tooling, and processes for how we build our product, ensuring technical debt is managed and developer velocity is optimized.
Department Representation: Represent engineering in key initiatives and projects within the department or across the company, ensuring they get delivered successfully.
Organizational Design: Design the organization, establish clear objectives, and maintain a high standard in people, delivery, and technology.

s.h: You Will Thrive in This Role If You
s.t:
Are a Technologist at Heart: You have concrete software development experience in your background and maintain a sharp, active interest in technology. While you won't be on the critical path for daily feature delivery, you aren't afraid to roll up your sleeves, dig into the technical details, and go back to the grounds to help the team unblock complex technical challenges. You speak the language of engineers fluently, using your technical depth to actively train, upskill, and elevate the team.
Drive AI Transformation & Adaptability: You are highly adaptive to change and actively embrace AI-driven ways of working (such as leveraging AI coding assistants, automated testing, and LLM tooling to optimize workflows). Ideally, you have successfully championed this shift in a previous role and can enthusiastically coach and help our teams accelerate their own AI transformation.
Have a Passion for People Management & Coaching: You transitioned into leadership because you genuinely care about people, culture, and team dynamics. You treat every challenge as a coaching opportunity, whether pairing with a developer or mapping out a career framework.
Collaborate Cross-Functionally: You like to work with cross-functional teams and other stakeholders to align engineering functions with product and business direction. Each of our teams is made up of "co-founders" from Product and Engineering—joined by designers, coders, and commercial minds. You optimize for both customers and the business.
Optimize Processes & Remove Roadblocks: You enjoy the design and optimization of teams to maximize their efficiency. You are comfortable stepping deeply into technical discussions to guide architectural decisions, or taking important stakeholder meetings to clear obstacles.
Are an Exceptional Communicator: You bridge the gap between deep technical execution and commercial strategy, communicating with absolute clarity to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high.

With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

The Data & AI Products and Data Serving teams are Pleo's two newest teams. Data & AI Products builds customer-facing features using data, AI or ML. Data Serving owns the production-grade data layer that every downstream consumer product teams, AI agents, and external customers depend on for clean, reliable data.
This Senior Manager role spans both teams. It is a data and engineering leadership role with a strong product backbone, designed for a builder-leader. You need to understand what good AI feature engineering looks like, what it takes to build end-to-end data products, data engineering best practice, and how to build and lead teams that do both well. You will stay close enough to the work to shape technical direction, unblock delivery, and raise the quality bar across both teams.
Who you’ll be working with and reporting to
You will report to the VP of Data and work closely with our Principal Data Engineer. You will partner closely with the Manager of GenAI Platform, Data Infra & ML Platform, Product Engineering leadership and Product Managers across Pleo.
What you’ll be doing

s.h: As a Senior Engineering Manager, you will
s.t:
Build, lead, and develop multidisciplinary teams as a hands-on builder of systems, standards, and team capability. In the Data & AI Products team you will find Applied AI Engineers, Data Scientists and ML Scientists while the Data Serving team is constituted of Backend Engineers, Data Platform Engineers and Data Engineers. We are looking for someone with a solid understanding of each of these roles.
Own the delivery for both teams: AI feature delivery for customers and the API and serving layer that underpins it.
Partner with product teams to define the AI feature roadmap. You are strategic partner to senior leaders across the business and can advocate for Pleo’s customers.
Drive quality and trust standards across AI feature development by implementing evaluation methodologies, production monitoring processes, responsible AI practices and more.
Ensure the serving layer meets the reliability and latency requirements of production AI features, product teams, and external customers directly accessing their data.
Manage resourcing and hiring across both teams through a period of growth.
Represent both teams in leadership and cross-functional discussions, translating technical progress and blockers into clear decisions needed.
Partner with the Manager of GenAI Platform to ensure product demand shapes the platform roadmap.
For more context, our tech stack currently includes AWS, Kotlin, Python, Kubernetes. LiteLLM, BrainTrust, Temporal, LLM APIs and more. You do not need to be an expert across all of these, but need enough familiarity to follow technical discussions and make good trade-off decisions.

s.h: You’ll thrive in this role if you have
s.t:
Proven experience leading cross-functional teams building AI-powered or data-intensive customer-facing products.
Technical depth in at least one of: AI product engineering, real-time reporting/analytics data APIs, or ML systems - enough to hold credible technical conversations and make good hiring and architecture decisions.
Experience building or substantially growing teams enabling you to hire, develop, and retain senior technical talent in a competitive market.
Strong product and business acumen. You can work with PMs and designers to shape a roadmap, not just execute one handed to you.
Track record shipping with quality under velocity pressure (AI features and production APIs both carry high trust requirements from customers).
Comfortable managing across distinct team mandates having different profiles, stakeholders and rhythms.
Experience scaling teams from the ground up and operating through very ambiguous environments. Both teams are new at Pleo, the AI product space is fast-moving but we expect you to drive delivery through clarity.
Why is this role a good fit for you

s.h: This role is a good fit for you if
s.t:
You have experience building and growing highly specialised teams from 0 to 1. You will need to play a key role in hiring the right talent and deploying them on relevant pieces of work.
Your product engineering understanding is as strong as your understanding of the data space. You will need to operate at the intersection of both worlds to be successful in this role.
You keep up to date with technology changes and still get excited about doing hands-on work. You probably have been developing your own agentic solutions and are eager to make these available to a larger customer base.

s.h: This role is not a good fit for you if
s.t:
You are a people manager without technical conviction, or you prefer a coordination-only leadership role. These teams are working in a technically complex space and need a leader with a credible point of view who can engage with the work, not sit above it.
You want to manage a stable, well-defined function. Both teams are being built and the role requires significant judgment about what good looks like.
You are not comfortable with the cross-functional complexity of spanning two distinct teams with different engineering profiles and stakeholder groups.
How you’ll develop in this role

s.h: In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll
s.t:
Develop a clear picture of where both teams are, the gaps in capability and structure, and the most important priorities to unblock first.
Progress hiring across both teams and set team up for success.
Partner with Product, Principal Data Engineer and technical leads to establish a clear delivery rhythm, quality bar, and roadmap for each team.
Ship the AI features through Data & AI Products and establish an evaluation and monitoring baseline.
We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills.
The location
Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work . We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

You will own critical central data pipelines built on large-scale alternative datasets, including transaction data, email receipt data, B2B spend data, and other third-party datasets. Your team will transform complex data into reliable, production-grade assets used by research analysts, product teams, and internal applications.
This role is ideal for an engineering leader who combines strong technical judgment, operational rigor, people leadership, and modern AI-assisted development practices. You should be comfortable using tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar systems to accelerate implementation, code review, testing, documentation, debugging, and technical exploration while maintaining a high bar for correctness, reliability, and production ownership.
What You’ll Own
You will lead the data engineering team responsible for building and scaling data systems for all of YipitData’s businesses, including:
Large scale data pipelines built for the public investor business units, corporate investor team, and/or private investor team
Production datasets and analytical models used in research workflows, applications, internal products, and customer-facing deliverables.
Architecting data flows and data models to support various business stakeholders use cases focusing on accuracy, timeliness, and reliability.
AI-ready analytical datasets designed with the structure, metadata, documentation, and business context needed for effective use by AI agents..
Data quality and observability frameworks , including validation checks, freshness monitoring, coverage monitoring, outlier detection, and automated QA controls.
Technical execution across Databricks, Airflow, SQL, PySpark , and related data infrastructure.
Operational excellence practices across documentation, incident response, monitoring, reliability, and production support.

Lead, coach, and develop a global team of data engineers while staying close to architecture, design, code reviews, debugging, and delivery.
Partner with Technical Product Managers and Data leads to translate roadmap priorities, customer needs, and research requirements into scalable technical plans.
Build and improve scalable data pipelines, data models, and QA systems for various data products.
Collaborate with business stakeholders and PMs to support reliable delivery of data pipelines, incident resolution, methodologies, and operational improvements.
Use AI coding tools to develop and enhance methodologies, accelerate engineering execution, improve documentation, strengthen QA, support technical exploration, and raise team productivity.
Create clarity and momentum in ambiguous environments by breaking down complex data, research, and product challenges into actionable engineering plans.

8+ years of professional experience in data engineering, data architecture, big data development, ETL engineering, or related technical roles.
3+ years of managerial experience , including mentoring, team leadership, and supporting delivery.
Experience managing, mentoring, or formally leading data engineers or technical teams in a hands-on player-coach capacity.
Strong hands-on expertise with SQL, PySpark, Databricks, and Airflow or similar workflow orchestration tools and AI toolings.
Experience building, maintaining, or scaling business-critical data systems , including pipelines, production datasets, data delivery systems, or customer-facing data products.
Experience working with application teams with OLTP and OLAP use cases
Deep technical judgment across data modeling, distributed data systems, pipeline architecture, orchestration, data quality, observability, and production reliability.
Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills , especially with Product, Research, Operations, Client Success, Sales, and Engineering stakeholders.

Experience with alternative data or financial data , including consumer transaction data, email receipt data, B2B spend data, or other large-scale third-party datasets.
Experience supporting internal business stakeholders , including collaboration with leadership to aligned on strategic initiatives
Experience building data pipelines that support AI agents, LLMs, automated insight generation, or AI-powered analytical workflows.

You will partner closely with platform, SRE, and product engineering teams to advance a self-service delivery model where engineers can build, deploy, and operate services with minimal manual coordination.

Location: Remote, US (preferably in Mountain Time Zone) Employment Type: Full-Time Switchfly is hiring a Director of Engineering. We build the loyalty and travel booking platform behind some of the world's largest airlines and financial institutions.

We want a leader who can see where travel and loyalty are heading as AI-driven discovery, conversational commerce, and new ecosystem models to reshape them, and who can build toward that future while delivering in the present. Coach Product Owners to grow from backlog managers into outcome-oriented thinkers, pushing them to connect features to business value, client impact, and measurable results. Work across the business, including Switchfly 's executive leadership and our clients, translating strategic intent into engineering scope with clarity and appropriate pushback. Guide the personal and career development of your people. Ensure teams work together and that each person has a voice.

Foster a culture that encourages learning, trust, and bravery. About you: 5+ years leading software engineering teams in Agile delivery environments, with a track record of owning outcomes rather than just managing process.

You understand how B2B2C businesses create value, where the client, the end user, and the platform's commercial model are three distinct things that all have to win. Consumer-only product instincts, however strong, are not enough here.

You are comfortable owning product direction, partnering with Product Owners to shape what gets built and why, not just how fast it ships. Customers trust Lambda with their infrastructure, workloads, and data. Security is foundational to earning that trust, and Identity and Access Management is at the heart of it – the control plane that determines who and what can access every Lambda resource. Enterprise and hyperscaler customers require the ability to federate their corporate identities, manage human and machine access, enforce least privilege, protect data with keys they control, and audit activity across their environments.
We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the Identity and Access Management team and define how identity, authentication, authorization, and key-management services are built and scaled across Lambda Cloud.

This team owns the foundational identity and authorization services on the critical path for every Lambda product – spanning APIs, Console, Kubernetes products, and cloud services – including identity federation, SSO, SCIM, users and groups, service and workload identities, RBAC, resource hierarchy, policy enforcement, and audit integration.
This is a technically engaged leadership role. You will own execution, team health, and organizational direction working with technical leadership on architecture, strategy and design decisions for services that must be highly available, low latency and resilient.
You will also drive alignment across Security, Product, Compliance, and customer-facing teams to build durable platform capabilities that are adopted consistently across Lambda’s services.
This role is ideal for an engineering leader who has built security-critical distributed systems and wants to shape the identity and access foundation of a fast-growing cloud platform.

Build, lead, and grow the IAM engineering team. Hire exceptional engineers, develop technical leaders, and create a culture of ownership and high engineering standards.
Work closely with the IAM technical leaders to define and deliver the long-term technical and architectural strategy for Lambda’s IAM platform.
Build secure, scalable identity capabilities for people, services, and workloads from federation and SSO to service and workload identity.
Evolve the authorization platform – RBAC, policy evaluation, and resource hierarchy with least privilege and auditability as defaults.
Make IAM easy to adopt across every Lambda service through consistent APIs, resource and action models, and integration standards.
Build and own Lambda’s Key Management Service, including customer-managed keys, HSM-backed protection, key lifecycle controls, and integration across compute, storage, and networking.
Own the reliability, security, performance, and operations of mission-critical IAM services including observability, safe rollouts, incident response, and disaster recovery.
Translate enterprise requirements into durable platform capabilities, and communicate strategy, delivery, risk, and operational health clearly to senior leadership.
Balance the complexity and flexibility required for enterprise-grade IAM with simple, intuitive experiences for customers with varying levels of identity and access expertise.

Have built and operated large-scale distributed systems with high availability, security, and reliability requirements.
Bring strong technical judgment across cloud infrastructure and IAM — authentication, authorization, workload identity, privileged access, and policy enforcement.
Can engage deeply in architecture, pressure-test designs, and guide tradeoffs across security, correctness, scale, performance, and operability.

2+ years of experience managing engineers, with a track record of hiring and growing strong technical teams
Strong background across two or more of endpoint security, network security, enterprise application security, and identity and access management

Experience with one or more policy-as-code or authorization frameworks (OPA/Rego, Cedar, Zanzibar/ReBAC)

About The Team The Live Ad Insertions team sits at the intersection of broadcast engineering, streaming infrastructure, and digital advertising.

Our mission is to deliver a seamless, high-reliability ad insertion experience across live and linear streams, from primetime tentpole events like the NFL and live sports to 24/7 linear feeds and breaking news.

We own the full stack of tools, systems, and operational infrastructure required to trigger, stitch, monitor, and verify ad breaks in real time at scale, without compromising the member experience. Live advertising is one of the highest-stakes, highest-reward surfaces in CTV.

When tens of millions of concurrent viewers are watching a single event, there are no second chances. A break happens once, in real time, and the window to act is measured in seconds.

That demands more than reliable systems: it demands proactive observability tooling that can detect anomalies before they surface to members, and the ability to make real-time corrections mid-event when something does go wrong. This team operates with the precision of a broadcast NOC and the velocity of a software startup.

We are responsible for the technology that turns a live signal into a monetized ad experience, at scale, millisecond by millisecond.

As an Engineering Manager, You Will Lead a team of engineers building the real-time infrastructure, tooling, and operational systems for live ad insertion across server-side, client-side, and server-guided delivery models.
Own the reliability and operational excellence of ad insertion during 24/7 linear streams and high-stakes live events, including NFL games, live sports, and awards shows.
Define the technical roadmap for live ad insertion, including SCTE signal ingestion and validation, ad pod management, manifest stitching, slate handling, and ad decisioning integration.
Partner with ad operations, broadcast engineering, content delivery, and ad serving teams to ensure seamless signal-to-slot execution from ingest to client playback.
Drive hiring, retention, and development of a high-performing engineering team capable of operating in a demanding live environment.
Establish the on-call and incident response culture for live ad systems, setting SLAs and runbooks for break-glass scenarios during high-profile live events.
Contextualize your team's larger advertising strategy and translate business priorities into a technically sound, executable plan.
Serve as the technical authority in cross-functional discussions on live ad capabilities, representing the team to leadership, partners, and vendors.
Skills and Experience We Are Seeking Technical Skills & Domain Expertise
Streaming Pipelines & Architecture: Deep hands-on experience with live streaming pipelines (from ingest protocols like RTMP, SRT, or TS through to CDN) and ad insertion architectures, including SSAI, CSAI, and SGAI (HLS interstitials/DASH).
Broadcast Standards & Splicing: Expertise in broadcast signaling (SCTE-35, SCTE-104, SCTE-224) and manifest manipulation for ad stitching, alongside familiarity with master control and linear playout systems.
Ad Pod Construction & Encoding: Advanced knowledge of managing live break constraints, including slate/fallback handling, break reconciliation, and encoding constraints (codec/bitrate matching, frame rate alignment) to prevent playback artifacts.
Ad Tech Decisioning: Strong understanding of ad servers, DSPs, and VAST 4.x/VMAP in live contexts, with a focus on managing strict decisioning latency budgets, timeout handling, tracking event firing, and mitigating the cascading effects of decision failures.
Operational Tooling: Proven track record of engineering for high-availability, zero-downtime live events, including building operational tooling for ad ops (e.g., real-time fill rate tracking, signal health visualization, and break monitoring workflows).
Leadership and Cross-Functional Collaboration
10+ years of total engineering experience with 3+ years managing software engineering teams in a live media, streaming, or ad tech context.
Strong track record of hiring and developing senior engineers in competitive talent markets.
Ability to operate in a flat, fast-moving organization, balancing long-term architectural investments against immediate operational needs.
Effective communicator across both technical and business stakeholders, including ad sales, ad operations, broadcast engineering, and executive leadership.
Experience collaborating with content and distribution partners, including MVPDs, vMVPDs, and broadcast networks, on joint live ad insertion implementations.

In this position, you will

Ensure the most effective frontend setup for the Marketplace. We have 40+ teams, each with 3 frontend engineers (iOS, Android, and Web) in the Marketplace unit. We know this will look different in two years. Deciding what different means, and getting 9 product domains to fund it, is the job
Drive Technology Strategy: Set and drive the future technology strategy for frontends, establishing a modular, scalable architecture that enables rapid development and strategic growth. Basically - raise the technological bar for all Marketplace unit.
Refine the domain's identity: Take sole ownership of shaping its future, successfully integrating Design Systems and engineering to treat our frontend platforms as a cohesive product.

Lead frontends: Lead a horizontal, platform-focused domain containing Android, iOS, Web, and Design System teams.

Elevate global UI quality: Integrate design systems and accessibility into the frontend ecosystem to consolidate technical, visual and interaction quality standards. Support UI experimentation.
Ensure Resilience & Reliability: Maintain robust release processes, Marketplace frontend quality, and performance monitoring to reduce downtime and ensure a consistent member experience.
Innovate & Optimize: Drive AI-efficiency enablement in frontend development and explore cross-platform frontend development opportunities to increase engineering speed and productivity.
A lot of this work will be influencing without formal authority : Champion the frontend technical vision among your director peers, influencing the leaders of 9 Product domains to accommodate and prioritize platform-wide changes across 40+ teams.

How much of a technical acumen? Enough to have in depth conversations with our direct reports. You will have 4 strong technical EMs reporting to you, as well as 3 world-class staff engineers. We don’t think you need to match their technical competencies (that’s a stretch!), but you have to be able to speak their language, understand problems at their essence, and be able to consolidate and multiply their inputs, including being able to disagree objectively.
Leadership: you have a track record of making level change in the organizations that you lead (rather than 20% change). Consolidating your team views and making coherent strategy out of those views is step one.

Step two is even more important: being able to implement these changes in your domain, and more so - across other domains in the marketplace - is a foundational ability you carry. In practice, that means you have at least 2 years of experience leading leaders and 5 years of experience influencing without authority.
Change horizon: You are comfortable holding two timeframes at once. We need someone who can say, "Here is what our frontend setup should look like in two years, and here is why" AND name the clear deliverable that has to ship in the first quarter to make that end state reachable. Leaders who only do the second are common. Leaders who only do the first are entertaining. We need both.
What this role is not: This is not a hands-on frontend or release-engineering role.

You will not be tuning CI, owning the release train, or reviewing architecture decisions yourself — you’ll have 4 strong EMs and 3 Staff Engineers close to the details, and your job is to turn their technical judgment into direction, alignment, and organizational change. If your strongest work is deep in the mechanics, you'll be underused here.

If your strongest work is changing how 40+ teams operate, you'll be busy.

At Superchat, we're rebuilding how businesses talk to their customers. The phone call, the contact form, the support ticket: all of it is being replaced by messaging and AI. We're building the platform that runs underneath.
Founded in 2020, Superchat has become the platform of choice for 10,000+ businesses worldwide , from globally recognized brands like Allianz, Auto1, Enpal, Danone, and GASAG to the small businesses, dental practices, and one-person startups that need to look bigger than they are. Today, millions of messages flow through Superchat every single day .
We started as a unified inbox: one place for every channel a customer might pick, WhatsApp, email, SMS, Instagram. Then ChatGPT happened, and the second chapter began: AI agents that respond across chat, email, and voice at the quality of the best human teams.
We're 100 people , profitable , and have raised €18M in funding (last round 4.5 years ago, we've been growing on our own money since). Headquartered in Berlin.
We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead one or more squads. You'll partner directly with the CTO to develop engineers, ship reliable software, and shape how our team works as we scale.
Who We Want
Experienced engineering people manager.
You bring 3–5+ years of people management experience in software engineering, ideally in B2B SaaS environments.
Strong delivery leadership.
You have a track record of leading squads of 5-10 engineers through full product and delivery cycles.
Technically credible.

Builder of strong engineers.
Your former reports got promoted, took on broader scope, or grew into roles that better matched their strengths.
Strong hiring instinct.

Comfortable with difficult conversations.

Clear communicator.

Who We Don’t Want
Pure delivery manager.
You treat engineering as a ticketing operation focused only on timelines and task tracking instead of product quality, technical health, and team growth. We need engineering leaders, not project coordinators.
Engineer escaping into management.
You moved into management mainly to stop coding rather than because you genuinely enjoy leading, coaching, and developing people. This role requires a real interest in people leadership, not retreating from technical work.
Top-down architecture owner.
You want to personally own architecture decisions alone instead of enabling strong technical ownership within engineering teams. Engineers own architecture decisions - you participate, challenge, and sponsor the right investments.
First-time people manager.
You are entering engineering management for the first time and have not yet experienced leading teams through performance, hiring, and scaling challenges. We’re looking for someone who has already managed engineering teams successfully.
Remote-only operator.
You prefer fully remote work and don’t want to actively build relationships and culture in person with the team. We believe strong engineering leadership requires regular in-person collaboration and presence in Berlin.

s.h: About the role: What's in the Box
s.t:
As the Engineering Manager for the Deliveries squad at HelloFresh, you will lead the engineering vision and execution for how customers control their box week to week. Your squad owns the systems that keep a subscription flexing with the customer's life: skip, pause and resume, reschedule, delivery cadence, delivery day, and address changes — the controls a customer uses before an order locks in at cutoff — along with the home and delivery feed that surfaces them.
Delivery planning is where correctness, resilience, and scale matter most: every change a customer makes must be applied accurately and in time before cutoff, and the platform must hold up at HelloFresh scale — around 7 million active customers across 18 countries, with close to 1 billion meals delivered a year. You and your team will work in a cross-functional squad with product, frontend, and data.
We are looking for a leader who brings deep backend engineering judgement and is energised by collaborating across disciplines to make HelloFresh better. We believe there are many different ways of developing skills and we love diverse experiences! So even if you don't “tick all the boxes” but think you'd thrive in this role, we'd really like to learn more about you.

Lead, inspire and grow a cross-functional team of engineers (backend and frontend), ensuring smooth delivery and continuous improvement of the Deliveries systems and tech real estate.
Own the architecture and reliability of the delivery-control experience — skip, pause and resume, reschedule, cadence, delivery day, and address — with a strong focus on correctness, applying changes in time before cutoff, data integrity, and operational excellence.
Drive design decisions for scalable, event-driven services (e.g., Kafka) that apply high volumes of delivery changes reliably, with the highest quality and resilience standards.
Operate as an engineering leader within a cross-functional squad: partner closely with product, frontend, and data to deliver end-to-end customer outcomes and make joint decisions across disciplines.
Champion observability, on-call health, and incident readiness so delivery changes stay accurate and available around the clock.
Actively contribute to hiring and capacity planning, conduct regular code reviews, and mentor engineers.
Drive a continuous improvement culture and promote the HelloFresh DNA.

You have led a team in an agile environment (5+ engineers), ideally within a cross-functional squad setup.
You bring 6+ years of hands-on backend development experience.
Deep experience building scalable microservices and event-driven systems (e.g., Kafka), especially where correctness, idempotency, and data consistency are critical — such as scheduling, subscription management, or other transactional domains.
Experience designing and operating high-throughput backend systems that other teams and customer-facing surfaces depend on.
Experience with DevOps practices and cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), including observability and production ownership.
A collaborative mindset and comfort working cross-functionally with product, frontend, and data partners.
You are an empathetic, strong communicator and active listener.
You are a self-organized individual who can operate autonomously, solve complex problems, and remove roadblocks.
You are a humble leader who can motivate a team and drive them to their highest potential.

You’ll receive a competitive salary package, including a HelloFresh-subsidized pension scheme.
Enjoy savings on your weekly HelloFresh box.

Since 2003, Entrata has evolved from a visionary, student-led startup into a global leader in AI-driven property management technology.

Today, we power the industry's most essential operating system, serving owners and residents worldwide through a comprehensive suite of intelligent leasing, payment, and communication tools powered by cutting-edge AI.

With a proven track record of sustained growth and a global team of more than 2,200 employees, we offer the rare combination of established stability and high-velocity innovation. Recognized by the Silicon Slopes Hall of Fame and the Utah Business Fast 50, Entrata fosters a culture of radical transparency and entrepreneurial energy.

At Entrata, we create an environment where different perspectives are valued and respected. Those perspectives challenge assumptions, strengthen our decisions, and raise the bar as we reshape the global living experience through AI-powered solutions.

Director of Engineering Payments provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for software engineering teams responsible for Entrata’s payments platform and money-movement capabilities.

This role establishes the technical strategy and execution roadmap for secure, scalable, and highly available payment experiences across card, ACH, disbursement, ledger, settlement, reconciliation, and related financial workflows.

Partnering closely with Product, Finance, Treasury, Risk, Compliance, Security, and external payment partners, this leader ensures solutions meet customer needs, regulatory and network requirements, and broader business objectives while remaining accountable for platform reliability, transaction integrity, financial accuracy, and risk reduction.

Reponsibilites
Direct the activities of multiple integrated software engineering teams, primarily through lower management levels .
Oversee the design, development, and delivery of software solutions driving enterprise-level transformation products .
Establish operational objectives, strategic plans, and technical design roadmaps for the engineering department aligned with long-term company goals .
Lead the architectural strategy and evolution of secure, resilient, and highly available cloud-native environments using technologies like AWS, PostgreSQL, and Node.js .
Direct the delivery of payment and money-movement capabilities, including payment acceptance, processing, disbursement, ledgering, settlement, reconciliation, refunds, returns, disputes, and exception handling .
Ensure platform architecture and operational practices support idempotent transaction processing, ledger integrity, auditability, observability, disaster recovery, and compliance with PCI DSS, NACHA rules, EI3PA, data privacy standards, and internal financial controls .
Partner across departments (Product, Finance, Treasury, Risk, Compliance, Security) and with external processors and banking partners to translate payment-network requirements into technical solutions .
Manage departmental budget accountability, strategic planning cycles, human resource planning, recruitment, and team performance .
Reconcile multiple stakeholder views and negotiate matters of significance to drive business results and maintain professional stakeholder alignment .
Establish and monitor key payment engineering metrics, including authorization and failure rates, processing latency, settlement accuracy, exception volumes, platform availability, and incident recovery times .
Leverage company-approved GenAI tools as a "Human-in-the-Loop" to automate routine tasks while maintaining data governance, PII security, and factual accuracy

Minimum of 10 years of software engineering experience, including at least 5 years in a significant engineering leadership capacity.
3 to 5 years of experience working with payment processing, money movement, fintech, banking technology, or other transaction-intensive financial systems.
Advanced knowledge of enterprise software architecture and cloud infrastructure, including Node.js, React, and AWS services (EC2, S3, IAM, PostgreSQL).
Deep understanding of card and ACH processing, payment gateways/processors, tokenization, authorization, settlement, reconciliation, refunds, returns, disputes, chargebacks, and financial ledgers.
Demonstrable experience leading teams that are leveraging AI-powered development tools (e.g., Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) for enhanced code generation, refactoring, debugging assistance, and overall development efficiency.
Demonstrated ability to lead engineering organizations responsible for high-volume financial platforms requiring transaction integrity, security, auditability, regulatory compliance (PCI, EI3PA, NACHA), and disciplined incident management.
Proven track record managing departmental budgets, strategic planning cycles, and recruiting/staffing technical teams.
Exceptional negotiation and influence skills with senior management and executive leadership.
Willingness to travel to client sites as needed.

Specialized expertise in database management and secure coding practices focused on Money Movement, Credit Risk, and Fraud prevention.
Demonstrated proficiency in prompt engineering and GenAI integration, with experience auditing AI outputs for brand alignment and accuracy while safeguarding proprietary data.
Demonstrated success leading large-scale technical transformations within fast-paced, high-stress, or heavily regulated environments.

AI frameworks like LangChain, LlamaIndex, and n8n are quickly becoming the default way developers build with AI — and MongoDB wants to be the data platform that shows up everywhere they build. As part of the AI Builders Experience org at MongoDB, we’re forming a brand new engineering team to make that happen, and we're looking for the founding Engineering Manager to hire the team, set the technical direction, and ship integrations into some of the fastest-moving open-source ecosystems in tech.
In this role, you'll be close enough to the code to jump into exploratory work yourself while also building the team, process, and operational rigor to keep a growing integration portfolio healthy long-term. The new team will work mostly in Python and TypeScript while collaborating closely with client library teams and other engineering groups across MongoDB that deliver the underlying driver, platform, and product capabilities needed to support these integrations well.
You’ll collaborate closely and move quickly with product, partners, field teams, the developer community, and open source project maintainers to ship where demand is real, deepen investment where adoption proves out, and evolve the portfolio over time as it becomes a critical part of MongoDB’s future in AI.
MongoDB engineering teams pride themselves on building high-quality software and living our values every day. We value intellectual curiosity, intellectual honesty, customer empathy, and building together in an environment that prioritizes collaboration over competition.
We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Gurugram for our hybrid working model.
Position expectations
Work closely with recruiting to hire a team of Python and TypeScript engineers who will build and own MongoDB integrations across a broad AI framework ecosystem that includes technologies like Langchain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, n8n, and Mastra
Execute effectively in a fast-moving environment where priorities may shift week to week based on framework changes, customer demand, partner needs, and strategic opportunity. Deliver quickly while keeping a high standard of technical quality
Flag issues, concerns, and resource needs early, working with management to triage, staff, borrow expertise, and cross-functionally hand off completed projects as needed
Work closely with product managers, program managers, sales, GTM, and peer engineering teams to define, prioritize, and deliver capabilities that improve the builder experience and strengthen MongoDB’s position in the AI framework ecosystem; help decide where to invest effort and where to pull back
Manage dependencies on drivers, platform capabilities, and other MongoDB product surfaces required to deliver excellent framework integrations
Collaborate with external teams who own open source projects MongoDB integrates with, maintaining a high standard of professionalism and courtesy to work effectively through external maintainer review cycles to land high-quality upstream contributions
Jump in to do initial, exploratory work. Guide key decisions, unblock the team, and contribute when needed as projects grow
Own the monitoring, operations, maintenance, and ongoing quality of a broad, evolving integration portfolio; develop testing strategy, release readiness, and operational follow-through after launch
Help the team build and maintain sustainable engineering practices, including CI/CD, automated testing, version compatibility awareness, and strong integration health over time
Develop a team that stays current with the Python, TypeScript, and broader AI builder ecosystems, including important frameworks, community discussions, and emerging patterns; maintain awareness of trends and discourse in contemporary AI
Bring a research and discovery mindset to the role, using customer, community, partner, and field signals to help guide roadmap and investment decisions; identify emerging opportunities in the ecosystem and help decide where early investment could create strategic advantage

8+ years of experience building developer platforms, libraries, or other high-scale technical systems, with strong proficiency in Python or TypeScript and an ability to lead teams working across both the Python and TypeScript ecosystems. Experience working with programming language polyglot teams is a plus
3+ years of experience managing a team of software engineers and providing technical leadership for complex projects or products
Experience with query optimization (especially MongoDB) and AI coding tools; distributed systems experience would be an asset
Demonstrated success hiring, mentoring, and growing high-performing engineering teams, including experience supporting career development, feedback, and performance management
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving technical landscape with frequent context switching, incomplete information, and competing opportunities, while maintaining sound prioritization and strong judgment
Strong technical depth in developer-facing software, with the judgment to make and guide architectural trade-offs
Experience leading the launch of new features or systems and operating them successfully in production after release
Excellent written and verbal technical communication, with a strong instinct to collaborate across engineering, product, and other stakeholder groups
A track record of escalating issues early and fostering a team culture that values intellectual honesty and collaboration
Comfort operating in ambiguous, evolving spaces and helping teams make progress when customer behavior, technical requirements, or ecosystem priorities are still taking shape
Strong and demonstrated interest in modern AI builder workflows and the developer tooling landscape, ideally with familiarity across frameworks, retrieval patterns, agent workflows, embedding, vector search, or adjacent areas; experience in this area would be an asset
Experience working with open source software, external ecosystems, or integrations with third-party frameworks and communities, especially in the Python ecosystem; familiarity with open source contribution models, external maintainers, and engineering work that spans company-owned and upstream repositories would be a plus
Success measures
In the first month, you will understand the team’s scope, the high-level architecture of the platform and integrations, the current portfolio of work, and the key technical and organizational dependencies around the role. You will start building relationships with cross-functional partners, especially recruiting, and develop a hiring plan
In three months, in collaboration with our recruiting team, you will have a healthy candidate pipeline and the first members of your new team onboarding. You’ll have a hand-off plan with the teams currently owning AI Framework Integrations
In six months, you will have staffed the core of your team, demonstrated effective partnership with recruiting, taken responsibility for major initiatives in the upcoming quarter, and improved the team’s ability to execute through technical and organizational ambiguity

Leadership and Delivery
Lead project delivery end to end, with clear governance, stakeholder communication, and accountability for outcomes
Build and mentor a high-performing AI engineering team, establishing technical standards and fostering a culture of quality and pragmatism
Own proposals and new business initiatives, defining technical feasibility and communicating risks and tradeoffs clearly to clients
Define what AI systems should and should not attempt, setting realistic expectations and being upfront about limitations
Conduct technical reviews and architectural assessments to maintain high standards across projects and team
AI Development
Guide the design and delivery of RAG systems, agentic frameworks, and LLM-powered solutions that are robust enough for production
Lead the application of advanced prompt engineering techniques including instruction design, few-shot sets, structured outputs, and tool/agent prompts
Run feasibility assessments to choose the right approach for each problem: prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, or classical ML
Mentor engineers on end-to-end AI system design and production deployment practices
Evaluation and Quality
Design evaluation frameworks including LLM-as-a-judge approaches, metric creation (recall@k, precision@k), and go/no-go gates
Lead structured experiments across prompts, retrievers, chunking strategies, and models, grounded in evidence not intuition
Establish team practices for identifying and categorising model failures including hallucinations, retrieval misses, and instruction-following errors
Set quality standards that ensure AI systems meet production reliability requirements
MLOps and Infrastructure
Build scalable inference infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines for AI/ML models that support rapid iteration and reliable deployment
Automate the full MLOps/LLMOps lifecycle: tracking, versioning, deployment, monitoring, and retraining across the team
Design APIs, microservices, and orchestration layers optimised for latency, cost, and reliability
Lead infrastructure decisions that balance technical excellence with business efficiency

2+ years of direct team leadership or technical management experience

Solid cloud experience across AWS, Azure, or GCP—preference for Azure—plus containerisation and orchestration knowledge
Hands-on RAG experience covering chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, and evaluation
Proven MLOps/LLMOps track record using tools like MLflow, Weights and Biases, or similar
Practical evaluation design skills: metrics, dataset curation, and structured experimentation

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. The Alarms team builds the response layer: the software that decides what happens in the minutes after an alarm fires. It uses real-time video, audio, and sensor data to analyze incidents, filter false alarms, and coordinate verifiable action.
This platform serves as the central intelligence for our alarm product, seamlessly combining AI-driven automation with human judgment to protect people and spaces at scale.
As an Engineering Manager, you will own this system across three surfaces: the customer incident experience, the monitoring software our human operators use to handle alarms at scale, and the integrations that carry an incident out to emergency dispatch.

Define where AI acts autonomously and where a human decides, in partnership with the product and our monitoring operations team.
Own the real-time workflow engine that models response actions after an alarm is triggered, and the vision-language pipeline that adapts SOPs mid-incident.
Set and hold the reliability bar for a system with no acceptable quiet failure mode.

Partner with the PM on the roadmap, and with the operators who use the monitoring tools daily.
Work across product teams to extend the response layer into the rest of the Verkada platform.

GenAI platform ownership: Own the platform the whole group builds on: LLM gateway, MCP gateway, agent platform, plugin marketplace, spec-driven development tooling, evals, and agent observability. Shorten the path from idea to running.
Forward-deployed engineering: Lead embedded engineers into marketing, HR, finance, and operations, redesigning each function's processes AI-native rather than simply automating them, shipping against a business KPI that function owns, and generalising each build back into the platform so the next team starts from a working pattern.

Strategy into roadmap: Co-create the group GenAI strategy with global central functions leadership, collaborate with the Product org to convert it into a sequenced delivery roadmap, and own the budget and investment decisions across tools and processes.
Team and engineering standards: Lead and develop Engineering Managers and Staff Engineers across Berlin and Warsaw, holding teams accountable for delivery, engineering standards, and team health, while scaling AI-native working practices into BAU.
Governance and cost: Keep adoption safe and affordable by owning guardrails, evals, model routing, cost control, and the compliance boundary with Security, Legal, and Procurement.

Engineering leadership depth: 10+ years in software engineering and 5+ years leading Engineering Managers across more than one discipline, with a track record of holding teams accountable for delivery and technical quality.
Agentic systems experience: You have designed, built, and shipped agentic systems with your own hands and teams, and you understand where they fail: context engineering, tool calling, agent orchestration, retrieval, and evaluation harnesses.

Technology strategy ownership: You have owned technology or AI strategy at an organisation or business unit level, including build vs. buy decisions, with the sequencing that takes pilots into production. You bring low ego, high ownership, and clarity over complexity to the decisions you hold.

Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.
Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. As a Director of Developer Experience, you will be tasked with leading the organization responsible for how every engineer at the company builds, tests, ships, and operates software.

You will own two interconnected functions: Infrastructure Services (CI/CD orchestration, GitOps continuous delivery, artifact management, and related platforms) and Developer Tooling (the teams that design and operate our CI/CD pipelines and internal developer platform).

Critically, you will also define and execute our strategy for integrating AI across the software development lifecycle, from AI-assisted code generation and review to AI-driven engineering intelligence platforms.
Developer experience is one of the highest-leverage investments an engineering organization can make, and AI is the largest shift in how software is built in a generation. The Director of Developer Experience will directly shape how hundreds of engineers spend their day, how quickly we ship, how confidently we operate in production, and how effectively we harness AI across the SDLC. This is a critically important role with executive visibility and a clear mandate to deliver measurable results.
What Will You Do?

Lead, grow, and develop a multi-team organization of managers and senior engineers spanning Infrastructure Services and Developer Tooling.
Define and execute the vision for developer experience, including build, test, deployment, artifact management, internal platform capabilities, and AI-augmented developer workflows.
Own the strategy and rollout of AI tooling across the SDLC, including AI coding assistants, AI code review and PR automation, AI-assisted test generation, and AI engineering intelligence platforms. Drive adoption, measure impact, and ensure these tools are deployed safely and effectively.
